pick.name: DocuSeal
pick.why: Most generous free tier checked (10 requests/mo cloud, unlimited self-hosted); API + embedding; no lock-in
pick.free_limits: Cloud: 10 signature emails/mo; self-host unlimited; Pro USD 20/user/mo

best_free.name: DocuSeal self-hosted (unlimited)
best_free.what: Self-host the open-source edition with your own SMTP
best_free.why: No signature limits, no per-seat fee; you run the server
best_free.free_limits: Unlimited signatures; you pay for hosting only

alts.name: Zoho Sign
alts.why: Low-cost mainstream e-signature inside the Zoho suite; also supports Aadhaar eSign for Indian counterparties

alts.name: Documenso
alts.why: Polished OSS option; free cloud 5 docs/mo

candidates.name: DocuSign
candidates.verdict: Best-known brand; buyers' legal teams accept it everywhere, but its pricing page returned 404 so cost is unverified

decision: DocuSeal's free cloud tier covers a small team's NDAs and order forms, and self-hosting removes limits. Pick DocuSign instead when a large enterprise counterparty mandates it, or Zoho Sign when an Indian counterparty needs Aadhaar eSign.

region_notes.US: Typed/click e-signatures are generally valid under ESIGN/UETA.
region_notes.EU: eIDAS recognises simple, advanced and qualified signatures; some documents need qualified ones.
region_notes.India: IT Act recognises electronic signatures incl. Aadhaar eSign; some documents are excluded.

verify.note: DocuSeal verified (cloud free 10 signature-request emails/mo, Pro USD 20/user/mo or USD 200/yr, self-host free unlimited, AGPL-3.0, release 3.3.4 on 2026-10-26). It is the best value, but 'best overall whatever the price' for counterparties' legal teams is arguably DocuSign (pricing unverified). Also best_free is the same product as the pick (self-host) - acceptable but say so.
